Article Title: 'I don't support the rally': Zohran Mamdani opposes RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's Madison Square event
Article Text:
Mamdani was responding to questions about the RSS, the proposed event and protests against Bhagwat's appearance.

Protests planned over Bhagwat event

NEW DELHI: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has said he does not support a planned event featuring RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at Madison Square Garden, while noting that the city may not have the legal authority to stop the private gathering.Bhagwat is scheduled to address around 5,000 members of the Indian diaspora at the iconic New York venue on August 29. His visit to the United States is part of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh 's centenary-year global outreach programme."I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,” Mamdani said at a news conference on Tuesday.Mamdani was responding to questions about the RSS, the proposed event and protests against Bhagwat's appearance. He was also asked whether the gathering should be cancelled.The mayor, who is the first Indian-American to hold the post in New York City, said his views were influenced partly by his family background.“I also stand here as the first Indian-American Mayor in our city's history, and my mother's family is all still in India," Mamdani said.He said his understanding of India was based on the idea of a society where people of different backgrounds could belong equally.He said the vision of India that he was taught by his family and the one that he grew up being very familiar with was that of "a pluralistic society, of a secular republic that believed in the belonging of each and every person who was from India".Mamdani said he was opposed to what he described as an increasingly exclusionary political movement.“And it has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision of any country, frankly, and so it is one that I find myself in deep opposition to, not only as an Indian-American but also as the Mayor of a city that believes deeply in the belonging of each and every person, no matter their colour, their creed, their religion, their faith, wherever they're from,” Mamdani said.The planned appearance has faced opposition from several interfaith and civil rights organisations. Groups including Hindus for Human Rights, the Indian American Muslim Council and the Interfaith Centre of New York held a press conference outside New York City Hall and called for the event to be cancelled.Bhagwat arrived in the US on Tuesday as part of the RSS's centenary-year outreach. During his stay in New York, he is also expected to participate in the Universal Oneness programme.The event is being organised by AHEAD Forum, which said in a social media post that Bhagwat would attend the Universal Oneness Celebration in New York on August 29.“The event carries a timeless and universal message: 'The world is one family'. It calls upon us to look beyond artificial divisions and differences, recognise the bonds that unite humanity, and embrace a spirit of mutual respect, harmony, and oneness,” the post said.Bhagwat's wider international tour includes the US, Canada and the UK as part of the Sangh's centenary-year global outreach programme.
Article Summary: Mamdani was responding to questions about the rss, the proposed event and protests. Bhagwat is scheduled to address around 5,000 members of the indian diaspora at madison square garden on august 29. His visit to the united states is part of the rashtriya swayamsevak sangh's centenary-year global outreach programme.

Article Title: 'Withdraw existing questionnaire': Kharge, Rahul Gandhi write to PM Modi over caste census issue

NEW DELHI: Congress high-command Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday urged the PM Modi-led government to change the way caste information is being collected in the census, warning that the current method could result in inaccurate data.The grand old party leaders also called for withdrawal of existing questionnaire, terming those "misleading".Kharge, Rahul requested PM Modi-led government to opt for a different way to detail on caste.In a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the two leaders said accurate caste data was necessary for implementing social justice policies. “The policies of social justice in India cannot be properly implemented without accurate data,” they said.Kharge and Rahul objected to the use of an "open-ended question" to record caste details. Under the system, people can provide the name of their caste, which is then recorded in that form.The Congress leaders said the same caste may be known by different names, sub-castes or local names in different parts of India. If these different names are recorded separately, “a single caste could end up being divided into thousands of names,” they said.They warned that this could lead to a very large number of caste categories and make the data generated by the caste census difficult to use.“If the correct number of members of a community is not recorded, its situation will also be assessed incorrectly,” the two leaders said. They argued that inaccurate data could affect backward, extremely backward and other disadvantaged communities.According to Rahul and Kharge, the impact could extend to government decisions on education, employment, welfare schemes and social justice.They also raised concerns over the lack of clarity about the size of country's Other Backward Classes (OBC) population. “We would not even know how large the OBC population is in India,” they said, pointing out that the term “backward class” is not included in the census process.Another Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also targeted BJP-led Centre over census. Ramesh said, "Government's current efforts towards a caste census are just whitewash".
Article Summary: Rahul, kharge write to pm modi over caste census. The grand old party leaders also called for withdrawal of existing questionnaire. The two leaders said accurate caste data was necessary for implementing social justice policies. Another congress leader jairam ramesh also targeted bjp-led centre over census.

Article Title: Donald Trump's volatility may have made India decline G7 presser
Article Text:
‘Unpredictable’ Trump behind no press conference after PM Modi meeting, govt says

NEW DELHI: Govt justified its decision not to have a news conference after PM Modi's meeting with President Donald Trump on the margins of the G7 summit in France, with official sources citing Trump's "unpredictable behaviour" at media events that have followed his meetings with heads of state/govt, including from South Africa and Ukraine.US ambassador to India Sergio Gor had earlier created a stir with his remarks about how ministry of external affairs had called to limit media interaction to photo opportunities and opening remarks without taking questions. Despite the request from MEA, as Gor had said, Trump went on to have a 45-minute unscripted news conference at the media event. Govt sources here stressed there was no unusual demand made by the Indian side.According to Gor, while MEA wanted to bring in the media, it said, "let's not do a full news conference".The ambassador’s disclosure of what might have been a private discussion is learned to have upset the govt. “Discussions regarding arrangements for public appearances of leaders are normal practice ahead of any VVIP visit,” said a govt source, on condition of anonymity. “Delegations when meeting Donald Trump are wary about his unpredictable behaviour, as may be seen from his interactions with president of South Africa, Ukraine, etc.Thus, the cautious approach by India,” he added.In highlighting Trump’s previous interactions with the presidents of Ukraine and S Africa, which devolved into televised confrontations with Trump hectoring his visitors, govt sources framed India’s request as a necessary safeguard against unpredictable diplomatic settings. The standard practice for govt has been to not have unscripted joint news conferences by Modi in company of the host or visiting dignitaries.This practice, though, has been questioned by local journalists recently in countries like Norway, the Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand.MEA defended the arrangement, stating that standard diplomatic procedures for international visits are followed.
Article Summary: ‘unpredictable’ trump behind no press conference after pm modi meeting, govt says. Us ambassador to india sergio gor had earlier created a stir with his remarks about how ministry of external affairs had called to limit media interaction to photo opportunities.

Article Title: India mulls annual dope tests on all commercial pilots on a random basis
Article Text:
File photo: A plane prepares to land at an airport in New Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Commercial pilots in India could soon be subjected to annual dope tests that may be conducted at random for the surprise factor. After the pilot in command of Air India’s Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight had reportedly tested positive, govt had directed the Directorate General of Civil Aviation to review the existing rules for these tests.“The DGCA is having stakeholder consultation right now on what the current regulation says and how do we ensure there is a strict policy around this (drug tests for pilots) in the future. This consultation is going on right now. There are multiple ways of approaching this dope test. So right now the rule says 10% across the overall pilot network but just like I said DGCA is engaging and one of the opinions from our side is that everyone has to go through it in the year at a random time,” Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said Tuesday.“We have to see how all the stakeholders are going to respond to this because one is the safety aspect of to ensure safety intact and the second is the operational impact. That also has to be taken into consideration.. We are going to balance both. If we do 100%, if every pilot has to go through the dope test once a year, then what can happen, what can be the impact of that, that is what DGCA is looking at,” Naidu added.Air India group has initiated a one-time dope test on all its pilots.Other airlines are also doing the same voluntarily, the minister said.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) is probing the why the Air India Airbus A320 had suffered a sudden loss of altitude by about 300 while operating as AI 2379 on Aug 4 from Phuket to Delhi which had left 20 passengers and four crew members injured. European aerospace major Airbus and France’s Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety (BEA) also joined the probe under AAIB whose report is expected in a week, according to officials.“Because everything is intact, the data recorder and everything is intact, the plane has also been in their possession…So I believe that we can expect some preliminary report very early from now,” Naidu said.
Article Summary: After the pilot in command of air india’s aug 4 phuket-delhi flight had reportedly tested positive, govt had directed the directorate general of civil aviation to review the existing rules for these tests. Air india group has initiated a one-time dope test on all its pilots.

Article Title: Did India hit Kirana Hills during Op Sindoor? Ex-CDS Anil Chauhan clears air
Article Text:
Chauhan also stressed that military decisions involve varying levels of risk and must be assessed against the political objectives they are intended to achieve

NEW DELHI: Former Chief of Defence Staff Anil Chauhan on Tuesday said India may have hit Pakistan's Kirana Hills during Operation Sindoor last year, but the strike was unintentional.Speaking at the ‘VIMARSH’ event on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath at the Vivekanand International Foundation, Chauhan said Indian loitering missions sent to search for radars around Sargodha ran out of fuel and ended up hitting Kirana Hills -- a site associated with Pakistan's nuclear facilities."At occasions, it's been asked whether Kirana Hills were hit or not, which is where their (Pakistan's) nuclear facilities are... Before those strikes, we had sent in a lot of loitering missions at Sargodha and Kirana Hills is about 10 kilometers north of Sargodha," Chauhan said."So the loitering mission is looking for radars which are in and around Sargodha, and it has a lifetime, which means it will loiter for about 2 hours and once it does not find a target, it comes down and hits somewhere. It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons as to what people asked, because Pakistani media also showed some kind of images in which there was smoke coming out from Kirana Hills," he added.Chauhan also revealed details of another episode during the operation, saying the Air Chief sought his approval to strike Sargodha after Pakistan requested talks. However the target was changed to Bholari due to bad weather."Once the Pakistanis had picked up the phone and said they wanted to talk at about 10 AM. The Air Chief asked me whether he should strike Sargodha, I said, Go ahead. I said, could you please identify two more targets, so one of the targets he identified was Skardu," Chauhan said."We gave a yes, but after some time, the weather was bad over it and they had to change over to Bholari," he added.During his address, Chauhan also stressed that military decisions involve varying levels of risk and must be assessed against the political objectives they are intended to achieve."Each option has a certain kind of risk involved in it, and also it will satisfy the political need for which it was to be used. So, it’s an interplay between risk and attainment of political objectives," he said.Chauhan said the operation remains relevant nearly 15 months after its major active phase ended. He said its assessment should take into account deficiencies identified during the operation, measures taken to address them and the changing nature of warfare.He added that these factors, along with wider global uncertainties, are creating new challenges for military planners.
Article Summary: Former chief of defence staff anil chauhan says india may have hit pakistan's kirana hills during operation sindoor last year. Chauhan said indian loitering missions sent to search for radars around sargodha ran out of fuel and ended up hitting the site.

Article Title: China's Xi Jinping to visit India with 400-member delegation for Brics: Report
Article Text:
Xi’s expected visit comes as India and China step up high-level talks to maintain peace along the border and rebuild ties. (File photo)

Chinese President Xi Jinping is likely to attend next month’s BRICS summit in New Delhi with a large delegation, more than double the Chinese contingent that accompanied him on his last India visit in 2019.Xi’s expected visit on September 12-13 with 400 officials, marking his first trip to India in seven years and comes as the two countries work to stabilise ties after years of tensions over their disputed border, reported Reuters, citing sources.Two Indian sources said Xi was likely to be accompanied by around 400 officials, compared with fewer than 200 during his 2019 visit. “Chinese officials are busy finalising hotels and security protocols,” one Indian source with direct knowledge told Reuters.Xi’s final travel plans and the agenda for any possible bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi are yet to be finalised, the sources said.The Chinese foreign ministry said, “China attaches great importance to and actively participates in BRICS cooperation, and supports India, the current chair, in successfully hosting this year's BRICS summit.”“We currently have no information available to provide” about Xi’s visit, it added.The expected visit comes as India and China continue high-level efforts to improve ties. National Security Advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday met Chinese Vice President Han Zheng in Beijing, with the two sides discussing ways to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and strengthen relations across economic, political and multilateral platforms.“On 25 August, NSA and Special Representative on the India-China Boundary Question, Ajit Doval called on Han Zheng, Vice President of the People's Republic of China,” the Embassy of India in China said.Read more: Ajit Doval’s China visit: NSA, Chinese VP Han Zheng discuss border peace, bilateral ties The two sides discussed strengthening peace and tranquillity in the border areas and improving bilateral ties “across economic, political and multilateral fora”, the embassy said.Doval is in Beijing for the 25th round of Special Representatives talks on the India-China boundary question with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The talks are expected to cover the border dispute as well as bilateral, regional and international issues.India-China ties were badly strained after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, in which 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed. The confrontation led to a prolonged military stand-off along the Line of Actual Control before the two sides reached a disengagement agreement in October 2024.Relations have improved gradually since then, with a series of high-level engagements between Modi and Xi. Their possible meeting in New Delhi during the BRICS summit could give fresh momentum to those efforts.
Article Summary: Xi’s expected visit on september 12-13 with 400 officials, marking his first trip to india in seven years. Comes as the two countries work to stabilise ties after years of tensions over their disputed border. Article Title: NSA Ajit Doval holds 25th India-China border talks with Wang Yi
Article Text:
NSA Ajit Doval with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. ANI

India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi on Tuesday held the 25th round of special representatives’ talks on the India China boundary question in Beijing, with the discussions focused on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the border and advancing bilateral ties.Earlier in the day, Doval met Chinese vice president Han Zheng ahead of the boundary talks. According to the Indian Embassy in China, the two discussed ways to strengthen peace and tranquillity in the border areas and further improve India China relations across economic, political and multilateral forums, in line with the consensus reached by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping.Chinese Ambassador to India Xu Feihong said Han highlighted the momentum in bilateral ties, noting that Modi and Xi had met twice over the past two years in Kazan and Tianjin and reached a series of important understandings. According to Xu, Han said these understandings had helped bring bilateral relations back towards recovery and improvement.Han also called for India and China to manage their relationship from a strategic and long term perspective, strengthen mutual trust, expand cooperation, improve multilateral coordination and properly manage differences. He stressed the need for sustained and stable development of bilateral relations.Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two day visit at the invitation of Wang Yi. His visit comes amid a gradual thaw in India China relations following a series of high level engagements between Modi and Xi.The two leaders had met on the sidelines of key international summits, including the SCO Summit in Tianjin, following their October 2024 meeting in Kazan. They had stressed that India and China are development partners rather than rivals and that differences between the two countries should not be allowed to become disputes.The ministry of external affairs had earlier said that stable India China relations based on mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity were important for the development of both countries as well as for a multipolar world and Asia.

Article Title: Repeated trips of Turkish military transport planes to Pak between Aug 19 & 21 raise eyebrows in India
Article Text:
Spike in Turkish military flights to Pakistan raises concerns over possible weapons transfers

NEW DELHI: An unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan in the last few days has raised hackles in Indian defence circles.Open-source flight trackers noted a 60-hour surge of Turkish military transport flights, including Turkish C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft (such as one with call sign TUAF526), landing at Pakistani air bases like Nur Khan, Masroor, and Murid between August 19 and 21.There is speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried Turkish military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems (drones) and air-defence equipment like Baykar (next-generation kamikaze UAV K2) and Asisguard systems (drone systems) to Pakistan. The aircraft movements were seen soon after after the signing of the tripartite Mecca Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia on Aug 7. The agreement establishes a collective defence pact, stating that an armed attack against any one of the three member states will be considered an attack against all of them.However, neither Pakistan nor Turkey has officially confirmed the precise nature or cargo of these transport operations.With Turkish aircraft landing in Pakistan, questions are being raised in defence circles whether Pakistan is gearing up for another conflict with India.Before Operation Sindoor in May last year, China and Turkey had allegedly supplied Pakistan with advanced military hardware, including Chinese PL-15 air-to-air missiles and HQ-9 air defence systems, and Turkish-origin Bayraktar (Yiha) and Asisguard Songar kamikaze drones. They also provided real-time battlefield data and tactical support.During the four-day conflict last year, the Indian armed forces tackled these attacks using their multilayered air defence grid and integrated command and control strategy, successfully intercepting all incoming aerial threats before reaching critical military or civilian infrastructure.The Indian forces deployed indigenous technology and advanced anti-access frameworks to crush the Pakistan defence network and also thwarted its offensive attacks. The IAF used long-range capabilities of Russian-acquired S-400 Triumf air defence system and indigenous Akash-NG missiles to thwart missile and UAV attacks. The IAF also used the S-400 to shoot down a high-value Pakistani Saab 2000 Erieye AEW&C surveillance aircraft from around 314 km away — which stands as one of the longest-range combat surface-to-air missile engagements in military history.

Article Title: Ex-IAF vice-chief Kapoor says India’s 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s, country must partner with global consortiums like FCAS or GCAP for 6th-gen programme

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air marshal kapoor (retd) did not totally rule out the role of tejas mk2 in future. Article Title: India, China to work towards political settlement of boundary question in long-term interests; Beijing stresses package solution
Article Text:
Ajit Doval and Wang Yi after the meeting.

Ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month, India and China held the 25th round of Special Representatives (SR) Dialogue on the Boundary Question, endorsing efforts to formalise the recent turnaround in the relationship on the back of border peace and discussing issues like de-escalation, boundary demarcation and border management.After the talks chaired by Special Representatives Ajit Doval and Wang Yi, while India said both sides agreed to work towards a political settlement of the boundary question in their long-term interests, Beijing also recalled a 2005 bilateral agreement to stress its proposal for a package solution.Doval was quoted as saying by the Chinese side that India and China are partners, not competitors, and developing a stable, predictable, and forward-looking India-China relationship carries great significance also for Asia and the world.“The normalcy we have witnessed in our relationship has been a direct result of both sides maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas,” said Doval, stressing the significance of border peace for further progress in bilateral ties. Wang, however, reiterated China’s position that the border issue must be placed in an “appropriate position” in ties.According to a Chinese readout, Doval and Wang held "in-depth communications" on advancing boundary demarcation negotiations, improving border management and control and promoting cross-border cooperation, while reaffirming their commitment to the 2005 agreement on political parameters and guiding principles for a "fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable package settlement" to the boundary question.China had dropped the mention of package settlement, which seeks a quid-pro-quo approach, in its readout of the last round of talks but had used it regularly for SR meetings earlier. Indian governments in the past, like in 2007 in Parliament, have said that they were exploring a "final package settlement" covering all sectors of the boundary under the 2005 bilateral agreement but India has not used that formulation recently, stressing instead on a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable settlement framework.On this occasion, the Indian government said in a statement that under the strategic guidance of PM Narendra Modi and President Xi, - in a constructive and forward-looking spirit – Doval and Wang had a candid exchange of views and agreed to continue their work in seeking a "political settlement of the boundary question in the context of their overall and long-term interests".The SR talks took place ahead of likely back-to-back bilateral meeting between Modi and Xi - first in Kyrgyzstan on the margins of the upcoming SCO summit and second at the BRICS summit that India will host on September 12-13. Xi is expected to arrive in India on September 12 for his first visit to the country in 7 years. While the schedule is yet to be confirmed, official sources said he will have a bilateral meeting with Modi and attend the PM's welcome dinner for BRICS leaders on September 12, before participating in the BRICS summit the next day.On the boundary issue, the Chinese side further said that both countries agreed to properly handle the boundary question through dialogue and consultation, jointly safeguarding peace and tranquility in the border areas.According to Beijing, Wang said that China-India relations have surpassed the bilateral scope and hold global and strategic significance and pointed to consensus reached in Modi-Xi metings in Kazan and Tianjin."China is willing to join hands with India to grasp bilateral relations from a strategic height and long-term perspective, strengthen communication, enhance understanding, resolve differences, overcome obstacles, and serve as good neighbors, friends, and mutually enabling partners, thereby realizing the vision of the Dragon-Elephant Tango," said Wang.Doval also called on Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng during the visit and discussed ways to strengthen peace and tranquility in the border areas and further improve bilateral relations across economic, political and multilateral forums.
Article Summary: India and china hold 25th round of special representatives (sr) dialogue on the boundary question. Talks took place ahead of likely back-to-back bilateral meeting between modi and xi. Xi is expected to arrive in india on september 12 for his first visit to the country in 7 years.

Article Title: H1N1 rising, but no cause for panic: ICMR DG
Article Text:
H1N1 accounts for nearly 98% of Influenza A cases currently detected in India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: H1N1 infections are rising across the country, but there is no cause for panic as the virus circulating is the familiar H1N1 pdm09 strain that has become a seasonal influenza virus, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) Director General Dr Rajiv Bahl said on Tuesday.H1N1 accounts for nearly 98% of Influenza A cases currently detected in India, while H3N2 accounts for only 2-3%, Bahl said. He stressed that the rise was consistent with the seasonal pattern of influenza and did not indicate a new or more dangerous strain.“Influenza is seasonal. It will keep coming every year,” Bahl said, stressing that the key concern should be a rise in severe cases, hospitalisations or deaths, rather than an increase in infections alone.He said it was too early to say whether the current rise had peaked. Viral infections typically rise, reach a peak, remain at a plateau and then decline, but the timing can vary by a few weeks.The surveillance network is testing samples from 73 sentinel hospitals for multiple respiratory viruses. The system includes testing for Influenza A and B, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus and other respiratory pathogens.A wider network of 167 virus research and diagnostic laboratories also undertakes diagnostic testing.Bahl said there was no need to test everyone for influenza. Testing is mainly required for patients with severe disease, for whom the result can help guide treatment.Most influenza infections are self-limiting. While most healthy people recover with supportive care, older adults, young children, pregnant women and immunocompromised people face a higher risk of complications such as pneumonia. Antiviral medicines may be prescribed for severe or high-risk cases, while antibiotics have no role in treating viral influenza, he said.On vaccination, Bahl said there was no urgent need for the general population to take the seasonal flu vaccine. People aged above 65 and those who are immunocompromised could discuss vaccination with their doctors. Influenza vaccination is not currently part of India's universal immunisation programme.He also said COVID-19 and influenza are circulating together, which is not unusual. Surveillance is continuing to track any change in the pattern or severity of disease.Basic precautions such as hand hygiene, covering the face while coughing or sneezing and staying home when unwell should be followed. Routine mask use is not considered necessary for everyone, Bahl said.The ICMR chief said the present rise in H1N1 infections did not constitute a public health emergency.
Article Summary: H1n1 accounts for nearly 98% of influenza a cases currently detected in india. H3n2 accounts for only 2-3% of cases, indian council of medical research says. The rise is consistent with the seasonal pattern of influenza and does not indicate a new or more dangerous strain.

Article Title: From 10% to 100%: Aviation ministry weighs annual dope tests for all pilots
Article Text:
The government is considering making annual dope tests mandatory for every pilot, instead of the current requirement covering 10% of the pilot network.

NEW DELHI: The aviation ministry is considering mandating dope tests for all pilots at least once a year, civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu said on Tuesday.The current rules require dope testing of 10 per cent of the overall pilot network, but the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is examining whether testing can be expanded to cover every pilot at a random time during the year.“There are multiple ways of approaching this dope test. Right now, the rule says 10% across the overall pilot network. DGCA is engaging, and one of the opinions from our side is that everyone has to go through it in the year at a random time,” Naidu told reporters.The minister added the government would need to balance aviation safety with the operational impact of implementing 100 per cent testing.“We have to see how all the stakeholders are going to respond to this because one is the safety aspect of it, and the second thing is the operational impact, which also has to be taken into consideration,” he said.Meanwhile, addressing the recent Delhi-Phuket flight incident, Naidu said the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) is investigating the incident and a preliminary report is expected soon.The minister said the flight data recorder and the aircraft are intact and in the possession of the investigating agency, which would help in the probe.“AAIB is presently taking up the investigation. Because everything is intact, the flight data recorder and everything is intact, and the plane is also in their possession, I believe that we can expect a preliminary report very early from now,” he said.Naidu also said the DGCA is holding consultations with stakeholders on existing regulations concerning substance use and ways to strengthen the policy.“More importantly, in terms of substance use and everything, DGCA is also having stakeholder consultations right now on what the regulation says today and how we ensure there is a strict policy around this in the future as well. So, this consultation is going on right now,” he said.The AAIB is examining the circumstances surrounding the incident, while the DGCA consultations are focused on reviewing existing regulations and strengthening safeguards related to substance use in aviation.The development comes after Air India flight AI2379, operating from Phuket to Delhi on August 4, experienced a sudden 300-foot altitude drop over Odisha, leaving 20 passengers and four cabin crew members injured.The Airbus A320, bearing registration VT-EXO, subsequently stabilised and landed safely in Delhi. The aircraft was carrying 137 passengers, including three infants, and eight crew members, comprising two pilots and six cabin crew.A purported post-flight maintenance report has also revealed a series of technical warnings involving the aircraft’s hydraulic systems, flight controls and autopilot during the journey.The report lists repeated low-pressure alerts across the green, blue and yellow hydraulic systems, along with low fluid levels in the yellow and blue reservoirs. Autopilot disconnections were also recorded twice.
Article Summary: The government is considering making annual dope tests mandatory for every pilot, instead of the current requirement covering 10% of the pilot network. The aircraft accident investigation bureau (aaib) is investigating the recent delhi-phuket flight incident and a preliminary report is expected soon.

Article Title: Ajit Doval’s China visit: NSA, Chinese VP Han Zheng discuss border peace, bilateral ties
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: National security advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday met Chinese vice president Han Zheng in Beijing, with the two sides discussing ways to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and further strengthen India-China relations across economic, political and multilateral platforms.The meeting came ahead of the 25th round of special representatives talks on the India-China boundary question between Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi later on Tuesday.Sharing details of the meeting, the Embassy of India in China said, "On 25 August, NSA and Special Representative on the India-China Boundary Question, Ajit Doval called on Han Zheng, Vice President of the People's Republic of China."The embassy said Doval and Han discussed ways to strengthen peace and tranquillity in the border areas and further improve bilateral ties "across economic, political and multilateral fora", in line with the consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries.Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two-day visit to participate in the Special Representatives talks with Wang Yi, who is also China's Foreign Minister.The talks are expected to focus on the boundary question, along with bilateral, regional and international issues.The Chinese Foreign Ministry has described the Special Representatives mechanism as the "main channel" for negotiations between the two countries on the boundary question and an important platform for communication on issues of mutual interest.The mechanism was established in 2003 to address the India-China boundary dispute, which stretches across roughly 3,488 km.The 24th round of talks was held in August last year, when the two sides held what Beijing described as candid and in-depth discussions and reached several common understandings.The upcoming round assumes significance as India and China seek to stabilise ties following years of tensions along the Line of Actual Control.The discussions come amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to gradually improve bilateral relations after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash and the prolonged military stand-off in eastern Ladakh severely strained ties.Doval and Wang had also met in June in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS National Security Advisers' meeting. The Ministry of External Affairs had described those discussions as "constructive and forward-looking".MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said, "The two sides reviewed recent developments in bilateral relations and noted progress towards gradual normalisation. NSA underlined that stable, predictable and constructive bilateral relations contribute to building trust and better understanding between the two sides. The discussions were constructive and forward-looking."The latest talks also come amid efforts by the two countries to build on a series of high-level engagements between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping.The leaders had welcomed positive momentum and steady progress in bilateral relations during their meeting on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin last year, after their previous meeting in Kazan in October 2024.They had reaffirmed that India and China are development partners rather than rivals and that differences should not be allowed to become disputes."A stable relationship and cooperation between India and China and their 2.8 billion peoples on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity are necessary for the growth and development of the two countries, as well as for a multipolar world and a multi-polar Asia befitting the trends of the 21st century," the MEA had said after the leaders' meeting.Despite the gradual improvement in ties, differences over the boundary and Arunachal Pradesh remain sensitive issues between New Delhi and Beijing.Both Doval and Wang are designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism. While the process has not resolved the long-running border dispute, officials on both sides continue to regard it as an important channel for managing tensions and maintaining communication.The talks also come ahead of Xi's expected visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit on September 12-13, which could provide an opportunity for another meeting between Xi and PM Modi and further discussions on the bilateral relationship.
Article Summary: Nsa ajit doval calls on chinese vice president han zhang ahead of border talks. Meeting came ahead of the 25th round of special representatives talks on the india-china boundary question. Doval arrived in beijing on monday for a two-day visit to participate in the special representatives talks with wang yi.

Article Title: ‘Constitutional monstrosity’: P Chidambaram attacks One Nation, One Election Bill
Article Text:
File photo: Congress MP P Chidambaram

Chidambaram disputes 2029 timeline

JPC receives suggestions on deferring state polls

Chidambaram had opposed Bills before panel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha member P Chidambaram on Tuesday said simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies cannot be held in 2029 even if Parliament passes the proposed One Nation, One Election (ONOE) legislation.Chidambaram, who appeared before the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the ONOE Bills, said his basic submission before the panel was that the proposed legislation violated the basic features of the Constitution, particularly parliamentary democracy in a federal country.In a post on X, Chidambaram said he was not permitted to disclose his evidence before the JPC but outlined the thrust of his argument.“I am grateful for the opportunity to present my views to the JPC on O.N.O.E. I am not at liberty to disclose my evidence to the JPC but the basic thrust of my deposition was that the Bill violated the basic features of the Constitution, especially the tenets of parliamentary democracy in a federal country,” he wrote.Chidambaram also rejected the reported assertion by JPC chairman PP Chaudhary that simultaneous elections could be held in 2029.“I have read the reported statement of the Chairman, JPC, that simultaneous elections are possible in 2029 I am afraid his view is wrong and goes against the text of the Bill,” he said.According to Chidambaram, the Bill provides that the “appointed date” can only be a date that comes after a general election. Since the next Lok Sabha election is due in 2029, he argued that simultaneous polls cannot be conducted in that year.“Even if the Bill is passed (which is very unlikely), the 'appointed date' under the Bill can only be a date 'after a general election'. The next general election will take place in 2029. Hence, simultaneous elections are not possible in 2029, which is a blessing,” he said.Chidambaram added that the Congress and other Opposition parties would launch a nationwide campaign against the legislation, calling it a “Constitutional monstrosity in parliamentary democracy in a federal country.”Meanwhile, the parliamentary committee examining the ONOE legislation received several suggestions during its deliberations on Monday.According to sources cited by news agency ANI, two public policy institutions proposed replacing subjective discretion in deciding whether to defer state assembly elections with defined and judicially traceable grounds, along with fixed outer limits for such deferrals.The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024, seeks to facilitate the proposed synchronisation of Lok Sabha and state assembly elections. The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, forms part of the broader legislative framework for implementing simultaneous polls.Both Bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha on December 17, 2024, and subsequently referred to the JPC for detailed examination.The panel has since held meetings with subject-matter experts and undertaken study visits, with its most recent study visit taking place in Lucknow in July.Chidambaram had appeared before the JPC on Monday and strongly opposed the proposed simultaneous-election framework.He argued that curtailing the five-year tenure of elected legislatures would violate the Constitution's basic structure.He also said he could not support the Bills on grounds of conscience and contended that the government did not have the two-thirds majority required to pass the proposed constitutional amendments, according to sources cited by news agency PTI.JPC chairman PP Chaudhary said Chidambaram had provided “good inputs” but noted that he represented a particular political party. Chaudhary maintained that the proposal to hold simultaneous elections was not against the basic structure of the Constitution.The ONOE Bills were formulated after a high-level committee headed by former President Ram Nath Kovind recommended holding Lok Sabha, state assembly and local body elections simultaneously in a phased manner.Historically, Lok Sabha and state assembly elections were held together from 1951-52 until the cycle was disrupted by premature dissolutions of some state assemblies in 1968 and 1969, followed by the early dissolution of the Fourth Lok Sabha in 1970.
Article Summary: Congress leader and rajya sabha member p chidambaram says simultaneous elections cannot be held in 2029 even if parliament passes the proposed one nation, one election (onoe) legislation. He appeared before the joint parliamentary committee (jpc) examining the onoe bills.

Article Title: ‘We can drive them crazy’: Rahul Gandhi takes aim at PM Modi, Amit Shah

In a statement suggesting that students’ protest and the Parliament session washout have the ruling BJP at a loss for strategy, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said “we” will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Kharge said Gujarat produced visionary leaders, but now “these two” are ruining everything.Rahul said the country is witnessing a fight between “those who give orders and those who want to express themselves”, adding that the country has started expressing itself after a lot of people behaved like “cowards” against the combine of RSS-BJP for a long time.“Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” the Congress leader said, adding “we will drive them crazy”.Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress, that seeks to create a common political strategy with non-Congress platforms of people’s struggle.Rahul said Modi is unable to sleep at night while Amit Shah, who was eulogised as Chanakya, did not come to Parliament for 20 days. “Because for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression. They realise this country will not stop expressing itself.It will break the RSS order.”“Till Modi and Shah give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep, we will keep them awake,” he said.He lashed out at the RSS as a “bunch of jokers”, and said the organisation has been reduced to being an instrument of big capital like Adani and Ambani, far from its original base of small businesses.The leader of opposition said Modi has messed up India’s national security and foreign policy, the latter because of the ignorant idea that he is making friends with the world leaders and foreign policy is about hugging them. He said Modi thought foreign leaders were his friends, and “they caught him”. He said India squandered a great opportunity presented by the Iran war to play the mediator, and the role was usurped by Pakistan.In what had the large audience from across the country in splits, Rahul illustrated Modi’s hugging by giving a bear hug to Rachnatmak Congress chief Sandeep Dikshit - who in turn asked Rahul jokingly “if he had thought he was hugging Italian PM Meloni”, and by enacting other practical jokes.
